newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire's AA-plus Fitch rating in doubt.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire's AA-plus Fitch rating in doubt.

text.p: As New Hampshire issued $63.7 million in 20-year obligation bonds, a bond-rating firm warned that two years of budget deficits pose potential problems for the state's bond rating.

State Treasurer Georgie Thomas told Governor Stephen Merrill and the Executive Council that the Dec 5 issue will fund projects authorized by the Legislature, refund 20-year bonds previously issued and produce hefty debt service savings estimated at $3.2 million.

But Thomas told state officials that Fitch Investors Service recently informed her the state's coveted AA-plus bond rating is in jeopardy. Two consecutive years of operating deficits for 1995 and 1996 make it necessary for the state to "take a look at what it is doing" she said.
The Legislature headed off the deficits by cutting expenditures and tapping $12 million from a $100 million health care transition fund that creates medical programs for the poor.
The new bond issue will provide $1 million for new projects and $9 million to cover a failed loan made by the state to Business Express Airlines.
The rest of the bond issue is for bond refunding, said Thomas.

The new issue makes the state's long-term net general fund supported debt at $465 million with $676 million in self- supporting dedicated revenues. The interest rate for the issue was 4.82 percent. The last time the state issued refunding bonds was in 1993.
